criteria.evidence: All four detailed-stage sections plus Agent intent (ICE) are present and substantive: e.g. Benefit hypothesis 'We will know it is true when: one play (`initialize`) asks the questions, each with choices and a proposed answer that names its source; ... the tracker has each needed type or a named stand-in'; Boundary has In, four Outs and four Nevers; Guiding rules has five rules; Features has six lines; ICE has Goal, Limit, Fails if, Context and Checked by lines.

Each edge and rule carries its reason: 'Never: make a work-item type in the tracker before the product owner's typed yes. A tracker is an outside system, and a write there is visible to the whole team.'; 'One run sets up memory, review rules and tracker types from the same answers. A second set of questions for the tracker or the review would ask the person the same things twice.'; 'Out: running a review and deciding its findings (the review play, /check-change, owns it). Initialize only records which rule groups fit; the review reads that record and names what it skipped.'

Every section is a list of discrete points; features state functions, not user stories: 'Choose the review rule groups (fn-review-rule-groups): records which rule groups of the review fit the project, so a review runs only those and names the groups it skipped.' ICE lines each start with one of the fixed labels.

The parent domain is a single directional Intent paragraph ('This domain turns a business intent into work that agents can build ...', marked 'To be deepened later'); the capability adds a measurable proof ('a review in the project runs only the rule groups that fit and its record names the groups it skipped'), named neighbour owners (/check-change, /shape-slice, /shape-plan, the install play), Never lines and six features. Detail clearly increases from parent to child.

Boundary: 'In: ... These five jobs share one moment (the project is being set up) and one input (the product owner's answers)' and 'Out: the install itself, which copies the plays, agents, skills and tools but brings no memory of its own (the install play owns it). Initialize starts where the install stops, so the two never write the same files.' versus Features: 'Lay Phoenix memory once, give each project its own blocks (fn-883): treats every memory file in Garura's source as Phoenix memory, has one install lay it on the machine and a second install bring it up to date, so `initialize` gives each project only the blocks its answers call for.'
criteria.fix: Resolve the edge contradiction around fn-883, and define its term. Either (a) add a sixth In line that names what this capability owns in fn-883 (for example: 'In: deciding which memory blocks a project gets from the Phoenix memory on the machine'), state that laying and updating Phoenix memory on the machine is done by the install play, and rewrite the fn-883 line so it names only initialize's part; or (b) move fn-883 to the install capability and remove it here. Change 'These five jobs' to match the In list once it is fixed. Define 'blocks' in one clause the first time it appears (for example: 'blocks, the separate parts of Phoenix memory such as one domain shelf or one standard'), so a cold reader knows what a project receives.
